mem.7:
Caroline (surname unknown) and Melanie (“Mel,” surname unknown) are friends who stayed in touch in 2023. Caroline is transgender; she began transitioning around 2020 and moved from her home country around 2019. Friends, family, and mentors support her. Melanie is married and has children.

**May 8, 2023:** Caroline attended an LGBTQ support group on May 7; hearing others’ stories made her feel accepted and more courageous about embracing herself. She hoped to continue her education and explore counseling/mental-health work. Melanie encouraged her, saying her empathy would make her a good counselor. Caroline shared a photo of a dog by a mural of a woman; Melanie liked the painting. Melanie shared her 2022 sunrise-over-lake painting, which she paints to express feelings, be creative, and relax. Caroline praised its colors and agreed art helps relaxation and self-expression. Caroline went to research; Melanie took her children swimming.

**May 25, 2023:** Melanie had run a mental-health charity race on May 20. She was trying to make time for running, reading, or violin; she was learning self-care matters and that caring for herself helps her care for her family, though it remained a work in progress. Her children anticipated summer break; the family considered June camping. Caroline was researching adoption agencies and hoped to become a single parent through adoption, a longstanding dream of giving children in need a loving home. She shared an agency photo; she chose it for its LGBTQ+ adopter support. She felt hopeful and optimistic, while recognizing the hard work of making the dream real was beginning. She was grateful for friends’ and mentors’ support. Melanie said she’d be an awesome mom and offered encouragement.

**June 9, 2023:** Caroline spoke at a school event the previous week about her trans journey, coming out, struggles, and personal development. She felt powerful; attendees related and were inspired to be better allies. She wanted to foster understanding, acceptance, hope, and a supportive community by sharing her story. Melanie praised her courage and advocacy. Melanie said her husband and children motivate her; Caroline called friends, family, and mentors her “rocks.” Caroline shared a yard photo of supportive friends she’d known for four years, since moving around 2019; they helped especially after a difficult breakup. Melanie shared photos of her husband and young daughter by a waterfall, and of herself in her wedding dress. She and her husband had been married five years (since around 2018). Another photo showed a family picnic with games and food. Melanie cherishes family time; both agreed time with loved ones brings happiness and gratitude.

**June 27, 2023:** Caroline shared a cross-and-heart necklace her grandmother in Sweden gave her as a child; it represents love, faith, strength, roots, and family support. Melanie shared patterned bowls and asked about treasured items. Caroline’s friend had made her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday (about 2013); its colors/pattern remind her of art and self-expression. Melanie’s family camped in the mountains around June 19–25: nature walks, marshmallows, hiking, and an amazing summit view; her two younger children love nature. Caroline was considering counseling/mental-health work, possibly with trans people. She attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop on June 23, learned about therapeutic methods and supporting trans clients, and was moved by professionals’ commitment to safe spaces. Her own journey and support groups helped her understand herself; she hoped to provide others a safe place to grow. She shared a bookshelf photo; Melanie encouraged her and shared her own bookshelf photo.

**July 3, 2023:** Caroline had attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade the previous week (June 26–July 2); the joyful crowd made her feel she belonged and showed community growth. She wanted to use her story to help others and was leaning toward counseling/mental-health work. She looked forward to a transgender conference in July. Melanie wished her a safe, fun trip. Melanie had signed up for pottery, finding clay creative, calming, therapeutic, and a way to express emotions. She shared a photo of someone holding a frisbee and a black-and-white flower-design bowl she made; Caroline admired it. Caroline was learning piano.

**July 6, 2023:** Melanie took her children to a museum on July 5; they loved the dinosaur bones. She shared a photo of two children at a water-play area and said it reminded her why she loves being a mom. Caroline was building a library for future children: classics, multicultural stories, and educational books; she shared the bookcase photo and looked forward to reading to them. Melanie’s favorite childhood book was *Charlotte’s Web*, for friendship and compassion; she shared its cover. Caroline said friends and family had given her love, guidance, and acceptance throughout transition, helping her accept and grow into herself. She shared a photo of women on a picnic blanket; she had picnicked with friends during the week before July 6. Melanie shared her family camping at a beach campfire; camping brings them closer.

**July 12, 2023:** Caroline said she attended an LGBTQ conference on July 10, felt welcomed and accepted, met people with similar journeys, and was motivated to fight for trans rights and awareness. She was still exploring counseling/mental-health jobs, inspired by the helpful support she received during her own mental-health struggles. Melanie shared a photo of a book with a gold coin on its cover, saying it reminded her to pursue dreams. Caroline loves reading; her favorite guide is *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, a true story about a trans girl and her family that gave her connection and hope. She took from it self-acceptance, seeking support, and the belief that hard times pass and love and hope exist. Caroline also shared a dog sitting in a boat. Melanie shared photos of her two girls with their dog and of their cat, saying pets bring joy; their pets are Luna (dog) and Oliver (cat). Melanie had bought pink sneakers for running and was running farther to destress and improve her mental health; Caroline encouraged her to keep prioritizing self-care.
mem.13:
Caroline (surname unknown) and Melanie (“Mel,” surname unknown) are friends who kept in touch in 2023. Caroline is transgender, began transitioning around 2020, and moved from her home country around 2019. Friends, family, and mentors supported her with love, guidance, and acceptance; their support helped her accept and grow into herself and was instrumental in her transition. She wants to pass that support on by sharing her experiences, advocating, and building a hopeful community. She values authenticity and is proud of how far she has come. She has explored counseling/mental-health work so people can have someone to talk to, and hopes to adopt as a single parent.

Melanie is married with three children. Her family motivates her, gives her love, and inspires her to be courageous. She finds peace in family and creativity. Pottery is a major part of her life, not just a hobby: clay calms and delights her and helps express emotions. She made a black-and-white flower-design bowl in pottery class and felt proud. She also paints. Flowers mean joy, growth, beauty, and appreciating small moments; they featured in her wedding decor and remind her of the day. Melanie and her husband had been married five years as of June 2023 (about since 2018).

**May 8, 2023:** Caroline attended an LGBTQ support group on May 7; others’ stories helped her feel accepted and courageous. She hoped to continue education and explore counseling. She shared a dog-by-mural photo; Melanie liked the painting. Melanie shared a sunrise-over-lake painting she made in 2022 to relax and express herself. Melanie was busy with work and children; Caroline went to research, Melanie took the children swimming.

**May 25:** Melanie ran in a mental-health charity race on May 20. Running, reading, and violin help her refresh and be present for family; she learned self-care helps her care for them. Her children looked forward to summer; family considered June camping. Caroline researched LGBTQ-friendly adoption agencies and felt hopeful and optimistic, while knowing the work was beginning. Melanie said she’d be an awesome mom and offered support.

**June 9:** Caroline spoke at a school event about being trans, coming out, struggles, and growth; listeners related and were inspired to be better allies. Melanie said her husband and children motivate her. Caroline calls friends, family, and mentors her “rocks.” She shared a yard photo of supportive friends she’d known four years, since moving around 2019; they supported her after a difficult breakup. Melanie shared family photos, including her husband and young daughter by a waterfall, wedding-dress photo, and picnic.

**June 2023:** Caroline and her trans-teen mentee attended a Pride event; she was encouraged by its love and acceptance, especially seeing the mentee’s face light up at the support. Caroline attended a Pride parade around June 26–July 2, feeling accepted, proud, and part of a growing community. Her grandmother in Sweden gave her a cross-and-heart necklace in childhood, symbolizing love, faith, strength, roots, and family support. A friend made her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday (about 2013), recalling art and self-expression. Melanie’s family camped in the mountains around June 19–25. Caroline attended an LGBTQ counseling workshop June 23; it inspired her to offer trans clients a safe place.

**July 2023:** Caroline had a picnic with friends during the week before July 6. Melanie took the children to a museum July 5; they loved the dinosaur exhibit, animals, and bones, and the outing reminded her why she loves motherhood. Caroline learned piano and loves reading; *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt gives her hope. Melanie’s pets include dog Luna and cats Oliver and Bailey (Bailey acquired by Aug. 23). Melanie took the children to pottery July 7; they made pots, including a dog-face cup, and painted a nature-inspired sunset/palm tree. They found purple flowers. Caroline attended an LGBTQ conference July 10, met people with similar experiences, felt welcomed, and strengthened her commitment to trans rights and awareness. Melanie bought pink running shoes and ran farther to destress.

Caroline’s adoption council meeting July 14 strengthened her resolve. Melanie shared sunflowers and roses in a blue vase. Caroline’s favorite color is blue (relaxing); sunflowers mean happiness, roses love and beauty. Melanie’s family camped July 1–2, enjoyed hikes, marshmallows, and campfire stories; she had a quiet, unplugged weekend July 15–16. The family enjoys camping, mountain hiking, and exploring forests to connect with nature and each other and make happy memories; they also enjoy the beach once or twice a year. Melanie recalled watching the Perseid meteor shower on a 2022 camping trip and making wishes. She cherishes her youngest daughter’s first steps.

Caroline joined an LGBTQ youth mentorship program and mentored a trans teen on confidence and positive strategies. She planned an LGBTQ art show for August and shared a tree-and-bright-sun painting inspired by unity at an LGBTQ center. Melanie and her children finished another painting like their earlier one by July 17. On July 18 Caroline joined a new activist group, Connected LGBTQ Activists; it meets regularly to plan events/campaigns, supports members, and gives them a platform to be themselves, support rights, and make a difference. Caroline finds it fulfilling and empowering. She missed the city Pride parade the prior weekend but saw it as proof equality and inclusion are possible. Melanie’s children flew a kite and made a sandcastle at the beach; seeing them happy was the best part. Melanie shared baby-in-crib and family beach-sunset photos. Caroline values family time and says family is everything.

**August 14:** Melanie celebrated her daughter’s birthday the previous night at a Matt Patterson concert; she loved his voice and songs and her children’s smiles. Caroline attended an advocacy event and Pride parade the previous Friday, energized by love, diversity, and acceptance. Melanie shared concert photos, including a band beneath an “all are welcome” sign; inclusion matters for their children.

Caroline advocates for LGBTQ acceptance through art, expressing her trans experience and helping others understand. Art helps her explore transition and her changing body, process experiences, and accept imperfections. She shared a painting of a woman with a cow in her lap and **“Embracing Identity,”** a woman in a red shirt symbolizing self-acceptance, warmth, and self-love. On Aug. 17 she described a hurtful encounter with religious conservatives on a hike; it reminded her of work still needed for LGBTQ rights. Supportive people reassure her she’ll be okay. Melanie shared a colorful patterned pottery bowl and described painting as a creative sanctuary that brings comfort, happiness, and fulfillment. They encouraged one another and expressed gratitude for their friendship. They fondly recalled a 2022 Pride festival photo of friends walking with balloons. They discussed a summer family outing and a separate nature outing together, but set no date or place.

**August 23:** Caroline applied to adoption agencies after attending an adoption advice/assistance group—the first step toward motherhood. She felt excited and nervous about parenting’s responsibility. She has a guinea pig named Oscar; a photo showed him eating parsley, his favorite. Melanie’s Oliver once hid a bone in her slipper; she also shared a photo feeding a horse a carrot. Caroline used to ride horses through fields with her dad as a child and has always loved horses. Melanie painted a horse on a wooden wall and likes painting animals. Caroline shared a recent self-portrait of a woman with a blue face; painting it made her feel liberated and empowered and helps her explore identity and be true to herself. She said freedom also comes from supportive people, advocating LGBTQ rights, and helping others live authentically. Melani
